---
title: Overview
---

A plugin is a Python package that adds something to **laplacekit**: a curvature,
a prior, a likelihood, a way to pick parameters, or a front door for another
library's models. Users install it and pass its objects where a built-in would
go:

```python
import laplacekit as lk

post = lk.laplace(
    model, loader, likelihood=lk.Categorical(), subset=lk.subnet.largest_magnitude(1000)
)
```

## Do you need one?

Often not. `lk.laplace` takes any object with the right methods, so a
likelihood or a subset defined in your own script works as it is. [Custom
likelihood](../quickstart/likelihoods.py) does exactly that. You need a plugin
when other people should be able to `pip install` your method, or when you want
it tested and versioned on its own.

## What a plugin can add

Each kind of contribution is a protocol in `laplacekit.core`. There is no base
class to inherit from, and `lk.laplace` never looks anything up by name: an
object with the right methods is accepted. If protocols are new to you, read [Protocols
in one page](protocols.py) first. The entry point a package declares
only lists it in `lk.plugins()` and `lk.health()`.

| Kind | Protocol | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [A subset](subset.py) | `Subset` | `lk.laplace(..., subset=)` |
| [A prior](prior.py) | `Prior`, `TunablePrior` | `lk.laplace(..., prior=)` |
| [A tuning objective](objective.py) | `Objective` | `lk.Minimize`, `lk.GridSearch` |
| [A likelihood](likelihood.py) | `Likelihood` | `lk.laplace(..., likelihood=)` |
| [A predictive](predictive.py) | `Predictive` | `lk.predict(post, x, method)` |
| [A curvature](curvature.py) | `Curvature`, `Staged` | `lk.laplace(..., hessian_approx=)` |
| [A function-space approximation](function_space.py) | `function_space.FunctionSpaceMethod` | `lk.function_space.laplace(..., method=)` |
| [A library integration](integration.py) | the above, plus a `ModelFn` | its own front door, e.g. `lk.diffusers.laplace` |

The rows go from the smallest contract to the largest. [Your first
plugin](first.py) starts at the top, with a subset, and ships it as a package.
Each row links to its guide, with a worked example and its test.

## First-party and third-party

Some plugins are first-party: the **laplacekit** author curates them as part of
**laplacekit**, and they come with an extra and an `lk.` alias. The rest are
third-party: anyone can publish one from their own repository. Mechanically the
two are the same:

| | First-party | Third-party |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Examples | `laplacekit-transformers`, `laplacekit-diffusers`, `laplacekit-subnet`, `laplacekit-heteroscedastic`, `laplacekit-reward`, `laplacekit-gp`, `laplacekit-marglik` | none listed yet |
| Curated with **laplacekit** | yes | no |
| Package | its own | its own |
| May import | `laplacekit` and `laplacekit.core` only | the same |
| Registers under `laplacekit.plugins` | yes | yes |
| Install | `pip install "laplacekit[transformers]"` | `pip install` with the package's name |
| Reached as | `lk.transformers` | an import of the package |

Apart from curation, only the last two rows differ, and both are
conveniences: a first-party plugin can do nothing a third-party one can't. [Plugin or pull
request?](plugin-or-pr.qmd) says when a plugin becomes first-party.

The [plugin list](index.qmd) shows the plugins we know of.
